theme: A coach's one quiet question turns a lost chess game into a professional habit: stop, look again, and name the real reason you lost.

grammar.point: 反而 / 却 / 竟然 / 居然
grammar.point_en: on the contrary / yet / unexpectedly / to one's surprise
grammar.structure: 反而 + 动词短语（与预期相反） ｜ 却 + 动词短语（转折） ｜ 竟然/居然 + 动词短语（出乎意料）
grammar.explain_en: Four words, two jobs. 反而 and 却 both mark a turn. 反而 means 'on the contrary': the result is the opposite of what the situation predicts, and the expectation is usually already on the table — 吃了药，病反而更重了. It often follows 不但不 or 不仅没, and it pairs with 更: 越忙反而越乱. 却 is the plainest written 'yet, however'. It sets two clauses against each other without claiming the result is surprising: 他说了对不起，我却没有生气. 却 cannot open a sentence; it comes after the subject and before the verb. 竟然 and 居然 both mark real surprise — the speaker did not expect this at all. 竟然 is neutral and slightly formal; 居然 is more colloquial and often carries disbelief or disapproval, and it works well in rhetorical questions: 你居然不知道？ Both stand after the subject and before the verb. A practical test: if the result contradicts what you expected, use 反而; if you are simply setting two facts side by side in writing, use 却; if you are registering surprise at a fact, use 竟然 or 居然. Do not stack them in one slot, and remember that 反而 often needs a partner such as 不但不, 不仅没 or 越……越…… to sound complete.
grammar.common_mistake: Learners put 却 or 竟然 at the head of a clause — 但是我却觉得, 却他没来. All four words sit after the subject and before the predicate.

examples.zh: 他吃了两天药，病反而更重了。
examples.py: tā chī le liǎng tiān yào bìng fǎn ér gèng zhòng le
examples.en: He took the medicine for two days and the illness got worse instead.

examples.zh: 我提醒过他三次，他却一句也没听进去。
examples.py: wǒ tí xǐng guò tā sān cì tā què yī jù yě méi tīng jìn qù
examples.en: I reminded him three times, yet he did not take in a single word.

examples.zh: 这么简单的题，他居然算错了。
examples.py: zhè me jiǎn dān de tí tā jū rán suàn cuò le
examples.en: Such a simple question, and he actually got it wrong.

drills.q: 我解释了半天，他不但没有消气，____。
drills.explain: 反而 is the fixed second half of 不但没有…… in this frame. 却 does not pair with 不但, and 竟然/居然 mark surprise at a new fact rather than the opposite of the expected result; both would also need 了 before the final particle.

drills.q: 这张表我昨天才发给他，他____已经填完交上来了。
drills.explain: 居然 marks surprise at a fact that was not expected, here the speed. 反而 needs an opposite result, 难免 predicts a natural consequence and takes 会, and 鉴于 introduces an observed situation at the start of a sentence.

reading.title: 那盘棋
reading.text:
我学象棋的那一年，输得很惨。教练从不骂人，只是在旁边看着，等一局结束后才问我一句：刚才那一步，你为什么那么走？

有一次，我明明看见对方的马已经跳到了危险的位置，却还是急着去吃一个小兵，结果输了。我很不服气，说运气不好。教练没有责备我，只是把棋盘摆回原来的样子，让我再走一遍，说是让我自己找教训。这一次我看清了：问题不在运气，在于我太想赢，反而忽略了眼前的危险。

那盘棋我记了很多年。后来工作里遇到类似的情况，急着抢一个看起来不错的项目，我竟然会想起那句问话，于是停下来，多观察一会儿。承认自己会犯错并不丢人；真正丢人的是，输了却不知道为什么。
reading.translation: In the year I learned Chinese chess I lost badly. The coach never scolded anyone. He just watched from the side and, once a game was over, asked me one question: why did you play that move? Once I clearly saw that his knight had already landed in a dangerous square, yet I still rushed to capture a small pawn, and lost. I was not convinced; I said it was bad luck. He did not blame me. He only set the board back the way it was and told me to play it again, saying I should find the lesson myself. This time I saw it: the problem was not luck but that I wanted to win so badly that I ignored the danger in front of me. That game stayed with me for years. Later at work, when I was in a hurry to grab a project that looked good, I would unexpectedly hear that question again, so I stopped and watched a little longer. Admitting you can make a mistake costs you nothing; what really costs you is losing and not knowing why.

options: 一盘输掉的棋带来的改变
怎样才能提高象棋水平
questions.explain: The passage moves from the lost game and the coach's question to the same habit showing up later at work, so the game's effect on the author is the subject.

questions.q: 作者认为那盘棋输掉的主要原因是____。
questions.explain: The author says '问题不在运气，在于我太想赢，反而忽略了眼前的危险', which rejects luck and names the real cause.

questions.q: 从最后一段可以看出，作者后来对“输”的态度是____。
options: 认为输赢一点也不重要
不再参加任何比赛和项目
questions.explain: The closing line says the real loss is losing without knowing why, which shows the author wants the reason, not simply the avoidance of defeat.

dictation: 那盘象棋我输得很不服气。
教练没有责备我，只让我再走一遍。
我太想赢，反而忽略了眼前的危险。
他一直在旁边观察，一句话也没说。
那次教训让我改掉了急着下结论的习惯。

writing.prompt: Describe a mistake you made at work and what you learned by going back over it. Use at least three of the words below.
writing.model: 刚工作时，我把一份报价单发错了客户，被经理叫去谈话。一开始我不太服气，觉得那只是小错。后来我们把整个过程重新走了一遍，我才发现自己在发送之前从没有观察过附件。那次的教训很简单：发出去以前停三秒，检查收件人和附件。经理没有责备我，只让我把步骤写下来贴在电脑旁边。那张纸我留了三年。
writing.tips: Set the scene in one sentence, show the moment you looked again instead of defending yourself, and end with the concrete rule you kept.
